title: Ground booking service in Java
idea: The core design is a BookingService facade that reserves court hours through a SlotLedger, prices them with a PricingStrategy, and charges through a PaymentGateway.

analogy.text: A club receptionist. They check the planner, read the rate card, take the card payment, and rub out the pencil mark if the card is declined.
analogy.breaks: The receptionist is one person; the service may run on many machines.

points: BookingService is a facade: callers use one method, not three collaborators.
SlotLedger reserves every hour of a booking, or none of them.
PricingStrategy prices each hour, so peak rules change without touching the service.
A declined payment releases the reserved hours before the error returns.

steps.caption: P-1 asks for court C-1 on Friday, 18:00 for two hours.
BookingService expands the request into hours 18:00 and 19:00 and picks id `BK-1`.
The ledger checks both hours, then writes both. Either all hours are reserved or none.
The pricing strategy prices each hour. Friday evening hours are both peak.
The gateway charges the total once. The charge succeeds.
The service returns the Booking with its frozen price.
P-2 asks for 19:00 on the same court. The ledger refuses, so nothing is charged.
P-3 gets a slot but the card fails. The service releases the hour before returning the error.

code.title: Service and interfaces
code.caption: Every collaborator is an interface passed into the constructor. Booking is a plain record here; page 4 adds status rules. PricingStrategy now prices one hour at a time, so mixed peak and off-peak bookings add up correctly.

walk.text: Wire the service: an in-memory ledger, peak and off-peak rates, a fake gateway.
Five requests: a booking, a clash, a mixed-rate booking, a declined card, a retry by another player.
Three interfaces, three swap points: who owns hours, how they are priced, how money moves.
`synchronized` makes check-all-then-write-all one step for this ledger.
Peak is a weekend or an evening hour. Each hour is priced on its own.
Reserve first, then price. A clash stops before any money moves.
A declined charge is undone: the hours go back to the ledger.

code.title: New rule, no edits
code.caption: A new pricing rule added as a decorator. The interface and PeakOffPeakPricing are copied unchanged from the core file.

walk.text: Wrap the existing strategy. Only court C-1, the turf, is outdoor.
Price three Tuesday hours on the indoor hall and the outdoor turf.
The interface is the one BookingService already depends on.
The decorator holds the inner strategy, the outdoor courts and the fee.
Ask the inner rule first, then add the fee for dark outdoor hours.

pitfalls: Do not charge before reserving; a clash after payment needs a refund.
Never put peak rules inside BookingService; that forces an edit for every rule.
Release reserved hours on every failure path, not only the happy one.

quiz.q: What does GroundBooking print for P-2's Tuesday booking?
quiz.why: Each hour is priced alone. 16:00 is off-peak at 50000 and 17:00 is peak at 80000, so the total is 130000.

takeaway: A facade calls swappable strategies; new rules arrive as new classes.

starters: Why reserve hours before pricing and charging?
When is a decorator better than a new strategy class?
How would I add a members-only discount to this design?
